messages.subject: New release: simmer 3.6.0 and simmer extensions
messages.subject_clean: New release: simmer 3.6.0 and simmer extensions
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

simmer 3.6.0 is on CRAN since a few days ago. The most interesting new feature is the implementation of the subsetting operators [ and [[ for trajectory objects.

We are also planning to release extensions for simmer. The first one is already released: simmer.plot <http://r-simmer.org/extensions/plot/> provides plotting methods for the core package (the ones previously present in simmer have been deprecated and will be removed). For the first time, simmer.plot allows us to plot diagrams of trajectories, which is very helpful for debugging purposes. Check out this post <https://www.enchufa2.es/archives/extensions-for-simmer.html> for more details.

We already talked about simmer.json a little bit in the past in this list, but its development is stalled right now. And Bart has been simmering a new interesting package called simmer.optim, which performs parameter optimisation. We would be very grateful if someone with experience on DES optimisation could try it out and give us some feedback. Simply install it from GitHub using ‘devtools’:

devtools::install_github("r-simmer/simmer.optim")

and start from the README <https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer.optim>, which demonstrates the current functionalities.

Regards,
--
Iñaki Úcar
http://www.enchufa2.es
@Enchufa2 <https://twitter.com/#%21/Enchufa2>

messages.subject: simmer.optim with schedule resource capacity and multiple generators
messages.subject_clean: simmer.optim with schedule resource capacity and multiple generators
messages.body_plain:
I'm developing a proof of concept for the simulation of Emergency Department patient flow and resource utilization. The already developed simulation model, using package "simmer", has multiple generators to reflect hourly variation of patient admissions and also a resource capacity variation based on the time of the day using schedule function.

Now i'm planning to get an optimal solution to the simulated scenario, and as result of my research i've get to know the simmer.optim extension. As i was studying it's usage and funcionalities, i saw that to experiment different solutions to get the optimal one, in the resource definition is necessary to set the capacity to .opt("xpto").
My question is: How can i keep a varying capacity definition during the day (using schedule) at the same time that i want to use the optimization extension? Problem is that the schedule definition needs the resource capacity to be defined has capacity=capacity_schedule for example.

Thank you in advance for your courtesy. Best Regards,

Bernardo Marques

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] simmer.optim with schedule resource capacity and multiple generators
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] simmer.optim with schedule resource capacity and multiple generators
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bernardo,

The .opt("something") instruction simply defines a parameter something that the optimiser will substitute with different values. You can place those parameters virtually anywhere in your model. That means that you may try something like this:
sim_model <- function() {
  # Schedule x units from 8 to 16 h
  #          y units from 16 to 24 h
  #          z units from 24 to 8 h
  capacity_schedule <- schedule(c(8, 16, 24), c(.opt("x"), .opt("y"), .opt("z")), period=24)

  ...

  env<-simmer() %>%
    add_resource("my_resource", capacity_schedule) %>%
    ...
  env
}

Then you can explore different ranges for x, y, z, i.e., morning, evening and night.

Also note that simmer.optim is in an early stage of development, so please double-check the results you get. And if you find something strange or you have ideas to improve the package, please fill an issue on GitHub.

Regards,
Iñaki
